messages:
maria: heads up — I'm prototyping a 'compatibility health' panel for the console to show per-route v1/v2 split + fallout. thinking signals: version header, fallback-rate, error-rate, and quota-churn. pinging eng/platform + product for thoughts

aj: quick Q — which version signal are we trusting? client headers can be spoofed (esp. via old proxies). if we use header-only we need a proxy-signed canonical header or correlate with auth token claims.

leo: +1 on signed header. we already add an internal header in dedicated proxy for routing: `X-RI-CLIENT-VERSION`. can we standardize that across hosted/dedicated/private?

dina: proposal: proxy adds `X-RI-CLIENT-VERSION` for all incoming requests (derived from handshake or auth token). also attach `X-RI-REROUTE-REASON` when fallback occurs. snippet: ```
# add header in routing proxy
req.headers['X-RI-CLIENT-VERSION'] = canonical_version
if routed_to_fallback:
  req.headers['X-RI-REROUTE-REASON'] = 'capacity:fallback' 
```

aj: another concern — billing attribution. if we transparently fallback to v2, token accounting often records the final model. we need to preserve the original requested version for cost/tenant impact reports. otherwise console panel will lie about who requested what.

maria: agreed — we should emit a metric label `client.requested_version` separate from `served.model_version`. billing events should reference `client.requested_version` for the tenant preview view.

leo: storing extra labels for every request might be heavy. suggest storing full KV (request headers + route) for a sample (1%) and aggregate counters for all requests. e.g. `counter.requests.by_requested_version` and `counter.requests.fallback_rate.by_requested_version`.

dina: that sampling approach sounds practical. Also recommend adding a small TTL trace for any request that triggers a fallback > 90th percentile latency so we can debug regressions.

aj: UX note — console panel should surface estimated monthly cost delta when switching tenant to v2 or when v1 is deprecated. Product wants a per-tenant impact preview before rolling deprecation.

maria: ok action items I hear: 1) standardize canonical header `X-RI-CLIENT-VERSION` across proxies 2) emit metrics `client.requested_version`, `served.model_version`, `fallback.reason` (aggregates) 3) sample full request payloads (1%) and capture full KV on high-latency/fallback anomalies 4) console panel + per-tenant deprecation preview with cost delta.

sam: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `proxy-standardize-header` -> canary=5% (route cluster alpha). ETA ~ 17m. :rocket:

leo: for telemetry schema let's use dot-namespace `telemetry.inference.request_version` / `telemetry.inference.served_model` so it's easy to join in dashboards. avoid reusing existing ambiguous names like `request.version` which people have already used differently.

dina: +1. also add a tag `telemetry.inference.fallback_policy` with values `grace|fallback|canary` so dashboards can filter by cause.

aj: can someone own an RFC? I can pick up the billing events piece (make sure storage pipeline attaches `client.requested_version` to usage events).

maria: I will write a short RFC and the console mockups. aj — please add a brief billing schema draft in the RFC. leo/dina — can you do a quick telemetry schema PR? I'll link the canary once it's green.

leo: will do a telemetry PR today. one more nit: add a console flag to opt-out tenant previews for privileged accounts (legal request).

maria: noted. decision: proceed with header canonicalization + sampled KV + separate billing label + console panel prototype. next sync if canary shows any misattribution. :thumbsup:
